name: npm-cli-pin
description: Hash-pinned npm CLI for sdk publish. Node 22 ships npm older than 11.5.1, the first release that can do GitHub OIDC trusted publishing. npm 11.21.0 vendors vulnerable copies inside its tarball, and overrides cannot replace those inBundle copies: brace-expansion 5.0.9, glob 13.0.6 (GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4), http-cache-semantics 4.2.0 (GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp), ip-address 10.5.0 (GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5), minimatch 10.2.5 (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249), postcss-selector-parser 7.1.4 (GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf), and undici 6.28.0 (GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx and four more). The newest releases, npm 11.21.1 and 12.2.1, still bundle vulnerable glob, minimatch, ip-address, and undici. The direct dependencies below are the patched releases, and postinstall copies them over the bundle. The lockfile records those pins so dependency scanners see the tree CI actually runs. http-cache-semantics is a local patch. A prerelease does not satisfy make-fetch-happen's ^4.1.1, so it is versioned 4.2.1 and the bundled lockfile entry records that. glob and minimatch were fixed only in new majors (14.0.2 and 11.0.1), and the advisories cover every glob 13 and minimatch 10, so no pin inside npm's ^13 and ^10 clears them. npm ci checks the ranges between bundled packages and ignores overrides there, so the lockfile entries of the bundled packages that require glob or minimatch add || ^14.0.3 or || ^11.0.3 to their range. npm only calls glob and minimatch APIs that both majors keep, and npm pack lists the same files with either. path-scurry 3.0.0 is the major glob 14 declares, patched in so the bundle matches it.
